gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 4-channel camera costs once the maker's own hardwire kit for parking mode is added: Vantrue N5S $323.98 (over $300), Vantrue Nexus 5 $295.98, Rexing R4 $299.98, Rexing R4-RD $279.99 with the kit in the box, REDTIGER VisionPano 40 $235.48.
standout_why: Compared against dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam (rank 1, cited) and dashlore.com/guides/best-dash-cams (both opened 2026-11-21), plus Rexing's R4 and R4-RD store text. Our own page gives every hardwire kit price as 'not stated (sold separately)' and has storage math for the REDTIGER F17 Plus only (46 Mbps, about 20.7 GB per hour, 6.2 hours on its 128 GB card). Dashlore lists only the N5S among 4-channel cams, with a 1,024 GB card limit and no hours, bitrate or kit price. Rexing's pages give camera and kit prices separately and never add them. No page sums camera plus kit against the $300 line, and none gives hours per card for the N5S. Not opened: Best Buy's R4 page, and the Tom's Guide and other roundups from the first chat. Standout is 2 rather than 3 because Botslab's store was unreachable, so the G980H's kit status and card hours are missing.
decides: The N5S fits under $300 only as a driving-only camera: at $293.99, any Vantrue kit that names it takes it to $323.98 or more. For a shopper who wants parking recording inside $300, the fits are the Rexing R4-RD ($279.99, kit in box, four exterior views), the Rexing 4-channel bundle with GPS, 64 GB card and kit ($259.99), the Vantrue Nexus 5 plus kit ($295.98, two cabin views, all three secondary channels 1080p) and the REDTIGER VisionPano 40 plus kit ($235.48). The Rexing R4 plus kit is $299.98 with no card, so it goes over once a card is bought. The Botslab G980H (our row) keeps the budget argument on camera price, but its parking-ready total needs a read of Botslab's box contents. On storage, the N5S works out to about 25 GB per hour, so roughly 10 hours on a 256 GB card and 40 on the 1 TB it supports; the Rexing R4 stops at a 256 GB card. Our live page also names the R4 in its short answer but marks the N5S as the table pick, which the rewrite should settle.

findings.label: Parking-ready price (camera + cheapest Vantrue hardwire kit that names the N5S)
findings.note: $293.99 + $29.99 = $323.98, which is $23.98 over $300. The kit (list $34.99) names 'N5 S' in its compatibility text. The 5-Level Adjustable Hardwire Kit, $34.99 (list $39.99), also names 'N5 S': $293.99 + $34.99 = $328.98 (https://www.vantrue.com/products/5-level-adjustable-hardwire-kit). The Universal 11.5ft ACC Hardwire Kit is $24.99 (list $29.99) and says it works only with Vantrue dash cams without naming models: $293.99 + $24.99 = $318.98 (https://www.vantrue.com/products/universal-11-5ft-acc-hardwire-kit). Every combination is over $300.

findings.source_title: Bundle: N5S + VP03 Hardwire kit + 256GB Card + CPL | Vantrue

findings.label: Storage use with all four cameras, derived from Vantrue's 1 TB claim
findings.value: about 25 GB per hour; about 10 hours on 256 GB, 20 hours on 512 GB, 40 hours on 1 TB
findings.source_title: How Vantrue's S1 Pro Max, N4S, N4 Pro S and N5S Dash Cams Differ (Michael Kahn, The Weekly Driver, 2026-10-06)
findings.note: Kahn reports Vantrue's claim as 'up to 40 hours on the N5S with all four' cameras on a 1 TB card; no resolution setting is given. Arithmetic: 1,000 GB ÷ 40 h = 25 GB/h; 256 ÷ 25 = 10.2 h; 512 ÷ 25 = 20.5 h. This is a maker claim relayed by a named reporter, not read on Vantrue's own page (HTTP 429).
